strings.string: Units, the automatic door and the heat guard. The watch is rated to 113 °F (45 °C); saunas and steam rooms are hotter, so you wear it at your own risk.
The watch thermometer notices when you go in and out. LAP always works too.
How much the watch must warm or cool before a round starts or ends on its own.
The band turns red and the watch buzzes every minute while its own thermometer reads this or more.
Rules from the occupational heat-strain criteria, each with its own switch. Not medical advice: on beta blockers or with a heart condition, ask a doctor and turn them off.
Come out when the heart rate stays high
After a full minute over the ceiling the watch buzzes and says so, once a minute.
Your age comes from your Garmin profile. Without one, the top of your zone 4 is used.
Longer cool-down if the heart has not settled
A minute after leaving, a rate still over the limit adds five minutes to the cool-down.
"Stand up slowly" when a round ends
Blood pressure sags after heat; this is the fainting moment.
RMSSD over each minute, from the wrist's beat timing, into the activity file. Sweat makes it noisy.
Dry heat, 170 to 200 °F. The guidance: rounds of 15 to 20 minutes, cool down at least as long as the round, 30 to 45 minutes of heat in a visit, several visits a week.
Wet heat, 110 to 120 °F. The guidance: rounds of 10 to 15 minutes, cool down at least as long as the round, under 30 minutes of heat in a visit.
The watch nags once a minute past this. 0 turns it off.
The break is never counted as done before the round before it was long. 0 turns the target off.
The watch asks you to come out once the rounds add up to this. 0 turns it off.
